facts.claim: Iora is a K2V dwarf, 0.82 M_sun, 0.33 L_sun, 4,950 K, 3.9 Gyr, rotating every 34 d, with no superflare in 2 Gyr.
facts.justification: Orbital life has no atmosphere to hide under, so a flare star would sterilise it; at equal flux a 4,950 K photosphere also gives about a fifth of Earth's UV.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Pigments absorb amber light peaked near 585 nm, so the biosphere reads magenta-black.
Exposed vacuum life persists for gigayears without atmospheric shielding.

facts.claim: Verrin orbits at 0.575 AU with e = 0.03 and 1.5 degrees inclination: a 176-day year and 1,360 W/m2 at the ring.
facts.justification: a = sqrt(L) puts Earth-equivalent flux around a 0.33 L_sun star; Kepler with 0.82 M_sun then gives 176 d.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Water chemistry is possible only because the flux matches Earth's.
The 176-day year fixes two eclipse seasons.

facts.claim: Verrin is a 0.30 M_J Saturn-class giant, 0.84 R_J, density 0.63 g/cm3, gravity 1.05 g, escape velocity 36 km/s.
facts.justification: Mass and radius are chosen together to keep density in the Saturn range; 0.95 R_J at this mass would be an impossible 0.43 g/cm3.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: The well binds ring material and makes ring escape expensive.
Saturn-class density puts the ice Roche limit just outside the ring edge.

facts.claim: Verrin spins in 10.5 h with 26.7 degrees obliquity and a 0.4 G equatorial dipole, ten times weaker than Jupiter's.
facts.justification: Fast rotation runs the dynamo; the weak dipole is deliberate, since a Jovian field would make the belts lethal.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Belt flux pulses on a 10.5 h radiation forecast.
The tilt sweeps the ring plane through shadow twice per year.

facts.claim: The ring spans 1.35-2.1 R_V, inside the ~2.17 R_V fluid Roche limit for 0.9 g/cm3 ice, with optical depth 1.2 and 20 m thickness.
facts.justification: A ring inside Roche is a body that failed to accrete, so its existence is derived, not asserted.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: The habitat is a 20 m sheet: a two-dimensional world.
Crossing orbits meet at km/s; co-orbital neighbours touch gently.

facts.claim: Coth is a rocky moon, 2,300 km radius, 0.31 g, 4.7 g/cm3, at 20 R_V every 16 d on e = 0.015 held by a 3:2 resonance.
facts.justification: Rock density is the only way to get 0.31 g at 2,300 km; the forced eccentricity dissipates of order 10^11 W, enough for a regional brine ocean.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Coth is the system's only solid viewpoint and only water source.
Tidal heat sustains a brine ocean under ice for gigayears.

facts.claim: The Ledge, Coth's L4/L5 swarm, is a co-orbital graveyard of captured ice bodies; L4 is a potential maximum where trapping is by Coriolis force.
facts.justification: The Lagrange points contain nothing themselves; what accumulates there is dead ice, not a nutrient cloud.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: The Ledge is loot, not a larder: arrival means mining.
Trojan orbits are predictable decades ahead.

facts.claim: Ring orbital speed is 21.6 km/s inner and 17.4 km/s outer, so crossing orbits close at km/s while co-orbital neighbours drift at cm/s.
facts.justification: v = sqrt(GM/r) for a 0.30 M_J primary; the shear makes every rendezvous a braking problem.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: An 8 km/s encounter vaporises both parties; safe contact is below 1 m/s.
Predation needs a phase change, not a chase.

facts.claim: Locomotion is reaction mass: an organism sublimates the ice it eats and throws it, so grazing and travel share one reservoir.
facts.justification: Momentum conservation in vacuum means every delta-v is paid with ejected mass; nothing supplies km/s for free.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Delta-v is the stamina bar and every approach is a braking problem.
Range is a function of appetite.

facts.claim: Radiation pressure at 0.575 AU is 9 micropascals on a reflector; a 10 g/m2 living sail accelerates near 1 mm/s2, enough to spiral outward, never inward.
facts.justification: P = 2I/c at 1,360 W/m2, and the thrust always points away from the star.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Sails are one-way tickets outward or a way to hold station.
A sail is a large reflector and advertises its owner.

facts.claim: The medium is granular vacuum near 10^-6 Pa with a mean free path of metres; sound is attenuated within metres.
facts.justification: At ring temperature the remaining gas is collisionless at organism scale, so pressure waves never reach a receiver.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Communication is optical, electrical or tactile; nothing you kill makes a sound.
Scent is a ballistic grain that arrives late and can be dodged.

facts.claim: Sunlight is 1,360 W/m2, zero in eclipse; Verrin-shine on Coth's night is 1.7 W/m2 at albedo 0.5.
facts.justification: Planet-shine scales as albedo times (R/d)^2, about a thousand full moons: dim but enough to see by.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Night is dim, not blind; hunting by planet-light works.
Silhouetting against ringshine is the standard detection trick.

facts.claim: Belt dose at Coth's surface is 0.5-5 Gy/day, and 10 cm of ice cuts it roughly a thousandfold.
facts.justification: A weak dipole at 20 R_V gives about a tenth of Europa's dose, and MeV electrons stop within centimetres of water.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Burrow 20 cm and live, or stay sail-thin and die young.
Exposure can be timed to the 10.5 h spin.

facts.claim: A ring organism sees a 1.7-2.0 h eclipse once per 6.5-12.7 h lap; the ring plane crosses the shadow twice per 176-day year.
facts.justification: At 1.35-2.1 R_V the planet subtends 96-57 degrees, so shadow is a sixth to a tenth of each lap.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: The thermal problem is dumping heat, not storing light.
Predators wait at shadow edges where prey must slow to cool.

facts.claim: Coth's ocean is water with 8% ammonia and salts at 180-230 K, pH 9, sealed by a clathrate-hydrate lid.
facts.justification: The ammonia-water eutectic at 176 K is the common antifreeze that keeps water liquid here; a clathrate skin holds about 1 bar of vapour.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Cells stay liquid near 200 K without freezing.
A puncture reseals as clathrate, so repair is chemistry.

facts.claim: Cryovolcanic plumes leave Coth at 300 m/s and 100-1,000 kg/s, feeding a dust-and-plasma torus at 20 R_V.
facts.justification: Plume speeds are Enceladus-like and cannot reach Coth's 3.7 km/s escape velocity, so they feed a torus but never ring speed.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: The torus is a refuelling station, not a launch ramp.
Plume phases are a calendar: water arrives on schedule.

facts.claim: Ring life arrived as impact ejecta: a 1 km impactor about every million years throws brine above Coth's escape while a fraction stays below sterilising shock; dust spirals in over 10,000-100,000 years.
facts.justification: Lithopanspermia is the only route that pays the km/s bill; electrostatic lofting lifts grains metres, so the ring is a colony, not a cradle, and ring abiogenesis is refused.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Every lineage descends from a launch event, not local chemistry.
Spores, not adults, are the dispersal stage.

facts.claim: The ring is 92% water ice and 8% silicate plus organics; at 221 K ice sublimes, and belt electrons radiolyse the top millimetre into hydrogen peroxide and hydrogen.
facts.justification: A warm ice ring loses mass to sublimation and is replenished by Coth's plumes; the peroxide frost makes food and poison the same material.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Peroxide above about 10 mM poisons; below it, it powers metabolism.
Grain rims differ chemically from cores, so milling depth matters.

facts.claim: Micrometeoroids strike at 10-40 km/s, and once a ring lane saturates its fragments become projectiles: the Kessler cascade.
facts.justification: Fragments are themselves projectiles, so one breakup can close a lane for years.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: A cascade is a disaster and a windfall of free matter at once.
Lane closure is a strategic map change lasting years.

facts.claim: The intracellular solvent is an ammonia-water eutectic brine at 176 K, held by a 1 mm clathrate skin resisting about 1 bar of vapour pressure.
facts.justification: Eutectic chemistry is real and matches ring temperature; the skin is the pressure vessel that allows a liquid cell in vacuum.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Metabolism near 200 K is slow and long-lived.
Freezing is survivable; boiling is not.

facts.claim: Primary production uses amber-light photosynthesis with magenta bacteriorhodopsin-like pigments peaked near 585 nm, the hydrogen/peroxide couple at about -340 kJ/mol, and direct electron capture from the torus.
facts.justification: A 4,950 K star peaks in the yellow, where retinal-based pigments outcompete chlorophyll, and peroxide frost supplies the oxidant.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Three metabolisms coexist: light, peroxide redox and electrotrophy.
Colour is magenta-black and advertises diet.

facts.claim: Food is ice, peroxide frost, UV-processed organics such as formaldehyde and methanol, and other organisms; poisons are peroxide above 10 mM, free oxygen, heat above 260 K, ammonia above 20% and impact plasma.
facts.justification: The same radiolysis that stocks the larder stocks the toxin, so every meal is a dose calculation.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Overeating peroxide is self-poisoning: a resource with a hard cap.
The warm inner ring is acid, not comfortable.

facts.claim: Reproduction is budding plus spring-loaded spore shells; tuns survive vacuum and kilogray doses, and gamete meeting in free fall must be aimed by orbital phasing, not by falling.
facts.justification: There is no sedimentation in microgravity, so gametes must be delivered; tardigrade tuns show the survival is measured biology.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Spore release is an aiming problem measured in metres per second.
Dormancy is the default stage; adulthood is the risky one.

facts.claim: From Coth the ring appears edge-on as a line spanning roughly 8-12 degrees, and ring organisms cross it at 17-22 km/s as moving lights: the night-sky egg.
facts.justification: At 20 R_V the ring's 1.35-2.1 R_V radius subtends that angle, and a lit body at ring speed crosses the line in tens of seconds to minutes.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Surface mythologies read the orbital biosphere as wandering stars.
The sky is a calendar and a warning system: a cascade is visible before it arrives.
